findings.summary: The eight-file runtime slice matches the CODEX-10-B handoff contract and engineering v1.2. It adds withSession inside the issuer→household→account→session transaction, five-field TEST-v1 record and withdraw commands, household-scoped digest receipts, epoch transitions that invalidate earlier active rows, durable throttles that can't move backward or be refilled, latest-row policy and epoch fences in play and entitlements, and consent routes on the existing hardened adult HTTP server. The protected controller probe exercises most attack and lifecycle paths against real PGlite, HTTP and services. However, the card explicitly requires app tests, and the delivered tests/loop-consent.test.mjs has only 3 tests that cover a small part of that list, so the result can't pass yet. Reviewer disclosure: I read the handoff instructions, the protected probe, the authorization record and all changed and relevant runtime code. I did not read all 1291 lines of PROJECT_CONTEXT v1.93 or the full engineering documents; I read only selected parts.

findings.title: Required app tests are largely missing from tests/loop-consent.test.mjs
findings.problem: The handoff makes these app-test requirements, separate from the controller-owned consent_probe.mjs: "Add app tests for both journal-boundary orderings, all old active epochs invalidated, wrong policy positives, disabled/expired/logout sessions, throttle global+household+window/backward clock, concurrent duplicate/new transitions and no leaks"; "Required app tests additionally prove A record/withdraw/reconsent leaves B status/epoch/receipts unchanged and vice versa; authenticated founder credentials ... authorize none of GET/POST consent or POST withdrawal; another household play and entitlement remain usable ...; Capture stdout/stderr ... assert no ... logged"; and "Required lifecycle app tests: ... Exercise both policy_mismatch and post-withdrawal rejection on fresh StartPlay, CommitAction, resume/read and actual entitlement write activateTrial/apply as well as readAllowance." The delivered file has 3 tests. They cover the two journal orderings, receipt snapshot and conflict checks, refusal while active, a check for old active epochs, logout and an expired session. They do not cover: any HTTP consent route (cookie, Origin, header, body or status mapping); founder-credential attacks; isolation between two separate households; policy_mismatch on play or entitlements; any entitlement fence (activateTrial, apply or readAllowance); CommitAction denial; global or household throttles, window reset or a backward clock; disabled accounts; trigger-based SQL rollback of permission plus receipt; withSession callback rollback; concurrent new transitions; changing optional flags while active without changing the epoch or denying play; or capturing stdout/stderr to check for leaks. A passing protected probe doesn't satisfy a requirement for repository regression tests, and missing evidence is not a pass.
findings.fix_check: tests/loop-consent.test.mjs (still the only test file) has app tests, using real PGlite, HTTP and services, for every listed item: the HTTP consent routes including founder cookie and adult-slot attacks; A/B household isolation in both directions; policy_mismatch and post-withdrawal denial on fresh Start, Commit, Resume, activateTrial, apply and readAllowance; a neighbouring household's play and entitlement still usable; global, household, reset and backward-clock throttles, with withdraw and refusal bypassing them; disabled, expired and logged-out sessions; SQL rollback via a trigger and withSession callback rollback; concurrent duplicate and new transitions; and a stdout/stderr leak check. The controller then reruns the full suite and it passes.

findings.title: Execution status file still reports blocked against the old base commit
findings.problem: The status record says state "blocked" with result_commit 84bbac3 (the pre-implementation base). REPORT.md says an actual candidate now exists and is awaiting feature review. The completion-record rule asks for exact revisions, and a stale status could mislead the continuous-mode controller.
findings.fix_check: The controller updates the status to the candidate's real state and result commit (7b6eac7 or its successor), without marking it accepted.

findings.title: REPORT lacks the exact candidate revision and downstream task IDs
findings.problem: The card says: "At completion record actual owner, artifact/PR or local output, exact revisions, checks, unresolved issues and downstream IDs from the index." The report gives the checks as run on "unchanged runtime source subsequently committed" but names no commit or tree SHA. It also doesn't list downstream IDs such as CODEX-02-C, beyond mentioning 02-C as future work.
findings.fix_check: REPORT names the exact commit the checks ran against and lists the downstream task IDs from INDEX.

findings.title: A withdrawn fixture row with an unknown policy reports policy_mismatch
findings.problem: projection() checks policy_version before state, so a trusted-fixture row that is both withdrawn and on an unknown policy shows as 'policy_mismatch' instead of 'withdrawn'. Access is denied either way, so this only affects how the state is labelled. Rows the service writes always use TEST-v1.
findings.fix_check: Either document the precedence in CONSENT_CONTRACT.md or decide which label should win; no change to access is needed.

findings.title: Throttle uses a second clock reading separate from withSession's
findings.problem: quota() calls now() again instead of reusing the 'at' that withSession used to check session validity, so one request can be checked against two slightly different timestamps. With the deterministic test clock this has no effect, but a single timestamp per transaction would be cleaner.
findings.fix_check: Optional: pass a single timestamp per transaction, or document why two readings are acceptable.
